blocks.text: Sulfur exhibits the oxidation states -2, 0, +2, +4 and +6. Its electronic configuration (Figure 12.8) shows that the oxidation state is determined by the number of unpaired electrons: with two unpaired 3p electrons sulfur is -2 or +2; promoting one 3p electron to a 3d orbital gives four unpaired electrons and +4; promoting a 3s electron as well gives six and +6. Under standard conditions sulfur and oxygen react to give sulfur dioxide, in which sulfur is +4; forming sulfur trioxide, with sulfur +6, requires high energy.

blocks.alt: Orbital boxes in four rows. a) Oxygen ground state 2s2 2p4: no d-orbitals in 2nd shell, so excitation is not possible. b) Sulfur ground state 3s2 3p4 with five empty 3d boxes: 2+ oxidation state due to two unpaired electrons. c) Sulfur 1st excited state 3s2 3p3 3d1: 4+ due to four unpaired electrons. d) Sulphur second excited state 3s1 3p3 3d2: 6+ due to six unpaired electrons.
